newsitem.title: USA: Treasury's Hawke says agreement on bank reg relief.
newsitem.headline: Treasury's Hawke says agreement on bank reg relief.

text.p: Treasury Undersecretary John Hawke said Friday contentious issues in the regulatory relief portion of banking legislation were worked out overnight and are now acceptable to the administration.
Provisions to bolster the Savings Association Insurance Fund (SAIF) were agreed upon some time ago, but some provisions to ease regulatory burdens on banks needed to be ironed out.
"This is the component where there were a lot of loose ends and I think those loose ends have now been tied up," Hawke said in a telephone interview.
"Our number one priority has always been getting BIF/SAIF done," Hawke said. "I think getting BIF/SAIF done now is a virtual certainty," he added.
BIF refers to the Bank Insurance Fund which insures deposits at banks and BIF/SAIF refers to the proposal to bolster the thrift deposit insurance fund.

"We think that the regulatory burden package is now in the shape that is acceptable. We think the compromises that were worked out last night strike a decent balance between preserving important consumer protections and relieving unnecessary burdens and keeping banks safe and sound," he said.
A key compromise worked out was related to the Truth in Savings Act and the requirement that banks disclose an annual percentage yield on savings products.
The banking legislation originally would have knocked out the provision allowing people to sue in federal court over the Truth in Savings Act, a spokesman for the House Banking Committee said.
Under the compromise, the provision permitting lawsuits in federal court would continue for five years and then be sunsetted instead of being repealed immediately, he said.
